articles.title: City sponsor Etihad Airways considering legal action against the Premier League
articles.summary: Airline ‘categorically rejects’ commission’s guilty verdict. Etihad has been club’s principal shirt sponsor since 2009. Manchester City’s main sponsor, Etihad Airways, is considering legal action against the Premier League following its publication of the independent commission’s core decision on…
body: In a statement released on Wednesday evening, Etihad said it “categorically rejects” the guilty verdicts of the independent commission, which it claimed had “damaging implications” for the airline, despite not being named in the published report.

The independent commission found City guilty of artificially inflating their revenues by £900m through “sham” sponsorship contracts that were secretly funded by the owners, the Abu Dhabi United Group.

Etihad, the state-owned national airline of the United Arab Emirates, has been City’s principal shirt sponsor since 2009 and was the main source of the initial transformation of their revenues. In 2011 City announced a 10-year naming rights deal worth £400m for the Etihad Stadium, which was subsequently extended on improved terms in 2021.

“Etihad Airways has reviewed the Premier League commission’s published opinion relating to the disciplinary proceedings involving Manchester City, together with the Premier League’s public communication of its findings,” the statement said. “Etihad categorically rejects any finding, conclusion or implication that suggests the airline has ever been involved in improper commercial arrangements.

articles.title: Hampton’s heroics preserve WCL point for Chelsea on Bompastor’s OL Lyonnes return
articles.summary: There were plenty of encouraging signs for Chelsea as they claimed a valuable point in the Champions League on their head coach Sonia Bompastor’s return to face her former team OL Lyonnes.
body: The goalless draw was a slow-burner but concluded with a flurry of late action where both teams missed chances to steal the points. However a draw felt fair on a night when Chelsea’s double pivot of Keira Walsh and Lexi Potter in midfield continued to flourish, three days after they similarly impressed in Sunday’s victory over Arsenal.

OL Lyonnes had scored eight times in their first fixture in the league phase, away against the Swiss side Servette, but Chelsea looked comfortable for large periods and Bompastor said: “I’m really proud of my team, being able to not concede here. We are happy also with the ball, the way we performed, we were able to exploit different spaces. The only thing that was missing was the goal.”

The French side had scored at least seven times in all four matches they had played in all competitions this season. Given that formidable form and the confidence in the hosts’ front line, Chelsea were grateful to Hannah Hampton for her sharp save from Salma Paralluelo on 20 minutes, and similarly glad to see Melchie Dumornay’s powerful effort fizz just wide of a post a few minutes later.

articles.title: Building of the Pep supremacy is an era that will be defined by sham-ball
articles.summary: Guardiola’s success at Manchester City was underpinned by financial cheating. Now he can only double down on his adherence to the owners. “Do you know the question that you are asking me?
body: Guardiola had the wind entirely at his back at this point, sitting in the Wembley press room an hour after Manchester City’s 6-0 defeat of Watford in May 2019. Success drowns out every other noise in football. To be good is also to be good, noble, virtuous. History is written by the domestic treble winners. Right up until the moment it isn’t.

The question in question was asked by Rob Harris of the Associated Press. It was basically this: information is now in the public domain that suggests Roberto Mancini received a second salary from Abu Dhabi when he was City manager. Mancini was one of Guardiola’s immediate predecessors. So had he, Pep, ever received two salaries?

Even as Harris was asking this he was interrupted by City’s press officer, saying: “ We’re not going here, we’re really just not going there.” A simple “no” would have done the job. Instead the exchange ended with another beautifully executed mad-dog stare from Guardiola; not angry, just sad and disappointed. But also, let’s be honest, really angry as well.

Now he can only double down on his adherence to the owners.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo walks out on Portugal after being dropped from starting lineup
articles.summary: Jorge Jesus earlier said captain would again be a sub. The 41-year-old has trained alone in gym since weekend. The Portugal captain, Cristiano Ronaldo, announced on Wednesday that he had left the team’s training camp in Denmark after head coach Jorge Jesus told reporters that the iconic striker…
body: Ronaldo had been due to train with his teammates at the Parken Stadium in Copenhagen on Wednesday but left abruptly after Jesus’s press conference. The veteran coach had said that Ronaldo, who spent the entire match on the bench against Norway on Sunday, would not start Thursday’s Nations League clash away to Denmark either.

“Following the national team coach’s press conference, and after having a conversation with the Portuguese Football Federation president, I decided to leave the national team’s training camp,” Ronaldo wrote on Instagram. “In due course, I will tell the truth to all the Portuguese people about my reasons for leaving the national team, to which I have always been dedicated.
“Now is time to wish good luck to Portugal and to all my teammates, without exception.”

Jesus had insisted earlier that there was no rift between him and Ronaldo, although the 72-year-old did acknowledge that his captain had been disappointed to remain on the bench in the side’s Nations League win over Norway.

articles.title: Meet the only Scot managing a national team in world football
articles.summary: More than 4,000 miles from his native Dundee, Kurt Herd is flying the flag for Scotland in international football - as manager of Dominica's national side.
body: The 34-year old is manager of Dominica, the Carribbean island, making him the only Scottish manager currently leading an international men's side.
"I'll be calling my mum and dad with that one," Herd laughs.
Appointed permanently in August after a short-term stint, Herd's role is not exactly like the one held by Steve Clarke, or his successor, Sebastien Pocognoli, though.

Herd is not just Dominica's manager but effectively their analyst, scout, nutritionist, and yoga instructor rolled into one, given he is the only full-time staff member for the team. Including the players.

articles.title: The five titles that got away as Evans seeks WRC glory
articles.summary: As Elfyn Evans looks to finally clinch the World Rally Championship title in Sardinia, BBC Sport looks back at the five times he finished runner-up.
body: Few leading sports stars have been so tantalisingly close to crowning glory for so long without achieving ultimate success as rally driver Elfyn Evans.
The 37-year-old from Dolgellau in north-west Wales has been runner-up in the World Rally Championship (WRC) five times in the past six years.
With this year's WRC calendar truncated by the removal of the planned Saudi Arabia finale, Evans takes a 17-point lead into the now season-ending Rally Italia Sardegna from 1-4 October.

If Evans can maintain his advantage over team-mates Sami Pajari and Oliver Solberg it will be a crowning moment for the Welshman, who would become only the third Briton to win the WRC title - joining Colin McRae and Richard Burns.

articles.summary: Manchester City's punishment for breaching Premier League rules should be handed down before the end of this season, senior football figures tell BBC Sport.
body: Manchester City 's punishment for breaching Premier League rules should be handed down before the end of this season, senior football figures have told BBC Sport.
The Premier League said on Tuesday that City had been found guilty of all charges relating to breaches of its financial regulations between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.
They included artificially inflating revenue by more than £900m through "sham" sponsorship deals.
City have repeatedly denied guilt and signalled an intent to lodge an appeal by the end of this week.

articles.summary: Michigan women's basketball landed a five-star recruit, who's a familiar name. CeCe Arico, a rising senior at Detroit Country Day and daughter of coach Kim Barnes Arico, pledged to join her mother's team earlier this week. The 5-foot-11 shooting guard is rated the No. 2 player in Michigan, the No.
body: Her sister, Emma, is on the lacrosse team at U-M while her brother, Trevor, is a student manager for the men's basketball team. Kim, meanwhile, is the winningest coach in program history – 312 wins across 14 seasons − and has more victories in Ann Arbor than any men's or women's basketball coach.

She's led the Wolverines to 13 different 20-win seasons as the women come off one of the best campaigns in program history, including tying a program record with 28 victories last year as the team made the Elite Eight for just the second time, both of which came under Kim Barnes-Arico's leadership.

articles.title: Price books Clayton showdown at World Grand Prix as Aspinall races through
articles.summary: Gerwyn Price set up an all-Welsh quarter-final showdown with Jonny Clayton with a straight-sets win over Ross Smith at the World Grand Prix, as Ryan Joyce and Nathan Aspinall also progressed in Leicester.
body: Price, among the tournament favourites after Luke Littler's shock early exit, followed his opening-round victory over Sebastian Białecki by dropping just four legs to despatch Smith at the Mattioli Arena.

The 2020 champion was outscored by Smith - having posted the highest average of the first round - but dropped just four legs during his 3-0 win, securing him a meeting with World Cup of Darts partner Clayton on Friday evening.

Clayton opened with three consecutive ton-plus checkouts and made four in total during a 3-1 victory over Wessel Nijman, where a 93.08 average and some remarkable finishing pushed him past the 12th seed.

Ryan Joyce breezed into the quarter-finals with a straight-sets victory over Danny Noppert, as Luke Woodhouse - who stunned Littler in the first round - was knocked out after losing 3-0 to Nathan Aspinall in a one-sided contest.

articles.title: US tennis star Navarro reveals health battle, ends season
articles.summary: American Emma Navarro, a three-time WTA tournament champion, revealed a three-year battle with health issues on Wednesday, battling against her body as she found success on the court.
body: Navarro, ranked 24th in the world, said she will skip the remainder of the 2026 campaign to prepare herself for a 2027 Australia return.
"I'm taking the rest of this year to work on dialing in my medication and fueling protocols so that I can hopefully feel back to 100% again," Navarro wrote in an emotional Instagram post.
Navarro won the WTA Strasbourg title in May, was runner-up in June at Nottingham and reached her fourth Grand Slam quarter-final at this month's US Open.
But the 25-year-old said her dizziness and headaches from under-fueling her body only faded for her to feel comfortable a couple of months ago.

articles.title: Somerset pair Overton and Luff win PCA awards
articles.summary: Somerset duo Craig Overton and Sophie Luff have won the headline accolades at the 2026 PCA awards in partnership with Toyota while emerging England stars Sonny Baker and Tilly Corteen-Coleman also received coveted honours at Exhibition White City.
body: Overton saw him collect a PCA awards quadruple, winning the PCA Men's Player of the Year trophy, the PCA Men's Domestic Overall MVP, the Rothesay County Championship Player of the Year and selection in the IG PCA Men's Team of the Year.

The 32-year-old, who has scored 951 runs, taken 76 wickets and 45 catches across all three formats this season, becomes the first Somerset player to secure the award since Nick Compton in 2012, beating competition from the notable shortlist of players including Joe Clarke, George Hill and Dan Lawrence.
He also scored a memorable unbeaten 79 in the Vitality Blast quarter-finals to take Somerset to Finals Day.
"It's a phenomenal feeling. To be chosen by your peers to win this award is very special; it means so much to me," said Overton.

articles.title: Gill hits 223 not out as India chase down 406 to beat West Indies in second ODI
articles.summary: A capacity crowd witnessed a host of batting records on Wednesday, Shubman Gill leading the way with 223 not out off 133 balls as India beat West Indies by eight wickets in their second ODI.
body: Gill notched his best ODI score and a record-high individual tally in an ODI run-chase. It was his 11th hundred in the format, one of five on the day, as India amassed 406-2 in 43.3 overs to take a winning 2-0 lead in the three-match series.
Opening partner Rohit Sharma made 101 as the duo put on 255 off 158 balls - the second-highest opening stand for India in ODIs.
It was the second successful 400-plus run-chase in ODI history, after South Africa's record 438-9 against Australia in 2006.

Earlier, three West Indies batters struck centuries in an ODI innings for the first time. Amir Jangoo top-scored with 114, skipper Shai Hope made 104 and opener John Campbell set the day's tempo with 101 off 68 balls.
